Après la compétition, le niveau d’un pil: After a competition, a pilot’s level changes by K × (score obtained − score expected), the score being the average of his or her duels (1 for finishing ahead, 0.5 for a tie, 0 for finishing behind). Beating weak pilots earns little (it was expected), beating strong pilots earns a lot, and losing to weak pilots costs a lot. A pilot’s level therefore does not rise simply because he or she wins often: the wins have to come against ever stronger pilots.

Avant chaque compétition, on regarde si,: Before each competition, we check whether, for two pilots already rated on at least 3 competitions, the one with the higher level finished ahead of the other. Over the whole history, this is the case for {p1} of the {n} duels. Among the 30 best pilots of each field (with at least 10 competitions), it is {p2}: the order at the top is hard to predict, and the gaps between the best pilots are often smaller than the uncertainty.

Chaque pilote a un niveau Elo avant la c: Every pilot has an Elo level before the competition. Each one is compared with all the others: for every duel, we look at who finished ahead and compare that with what the level gap predicted ({scale} points of difference = 10 to 1 odds of winning the duel). Beating a stronger pilot earns a lot, beating a weaker one almost nothing; losing to a weaker pilot costs a lot. Duels won is the share of opponents the pilot actually finished ahead of; Expected is the share the levels predicted. A favourite is never certain to win everything: at 85% expected per duel, he or she is on average beaten by about one opponent in seven (hovering over the column shows the resulting expected rank). The step size (K) is larger for pilots with few rated results.

Le classement est un <b>Elo</b> adapté a: The ranking is an Elo system adapted to paragliding competitions. Each pilot has a level, which starts at {start}. In a competition, every pilot is compared with all the others: for a duel between two pilots whose levels are A and B, the chance that A finishes ahead is 1 / (1 + 10(B − A) / {scale}). A gap of {scale} points corresponds to 10 to 1 odds.

Le niveau est mis à jour avec K = {k} ×: The level is updated with K = {k} × (1 + {boost} × e<sup>−n/10</sup>), where n is the number of competitions already rated for the pilot: new pilots move fast (up to K = {kmax}), veterans more slowly (K tends towards {k}).
Le numéro 1 est le premier des pilotes a: The number one is the top active pilot at the end of each month (inactive pilots are left out). The overall ranking is mixed; the women’s ranking only counts pilots whose gender is known.
Le rating est un niveau Elo : à chaque c: The rating is an Elo level: at each competition, a pilot gains or loses depending on the pilots he or she beat or not, taking their level into account.
Le site n’utilise aucun traceur ni mesur: The site uses no trackers or audience measurement. A single cookie, “lang”, remembers the chosen language (one year). Like any web server, the hosting may keep technical logs (IP address, date, page requested) for security, for a limited time. Pilot pages and search are excluded from search engines. No font or resource is loaded from a third-party site.
Le ± affiché à côté du rating est un éca: The ± shown next to the rating is one standard deviation: there is about a 2 in 3 chance that the pilot’s true level lies within this range. It equals √({f}² + {nw}²/(n + {c}) + {d}² × t), where n is the “effective” number of competitions and t the number of months since the last competition: about ±{s1} after one competition, ±{s10} after ten, and never less than ±{f}, because with a high K each competition also moves veterans’ levels. These values were calibrated by simulation: fictitious pilots whose true level is known fly exactly the competitions in the database, with random results tuned so that the ranking predicts as well as on the real data; we then measure the gap between the computed rating and the true level. The likely rank is the rank the pilot would have with their rating minus or plus one standard deviation, all other pilots staying in place.
Le ± est l’incertitude du rating (un éca: The ± is the rating’s uncertainty (one standard deviation: about a 2 in 3 chance that the true level lies within this range, drawn on the bar). It shrinks with the number of competitions and grows with time spent without competing. Hover over the rank to see the matching likely rank.

Un Elo ne compare que des pilotes qui se: An Elo system only compares pilots who have met, directly or through pilots in common. A pilot who only flies regional competitions is judged against his or her usual opponents; the level is linked to the rest of the world only through pilots who compete at both levels. Levels only mean something relative to each other (the average level drifts as new pilots arrive), and the gaps between the best pilots are often smaller than the precision of the estimate.
Un classement qui estime le niveau de ch: A ranking that estimates each pilot’s level from the results, competition after competition.
Un pilote sans compétition depuis plus d: A pilot with no competition for more than {m} months is inactive: he or she leaves the ranking. The level is kept and the pilot may be shown, greyed out and unnumbered, at the place that level would give, but takes nobody’s place: ranks only count active pilots. On return, the “effective” number of competitions is halved every {h} months of absence beyond the threshold, which raises K: the first results count for more. This rule is specific to this site.

A pilot with no competition for more than {m} months is inactive: he or she leaves the ranking (no rank, takes nobody’s place). When shown, he or she is greyed out at the place his or her level would give. On return, the pilot becomes “provisional” again: the next results will move him or her faster.
